title: Counit-normalized exceptional reduction comparisons respect quotient transitions
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and the coefficient categories $D^b_c(T,A_n)$ and $D^b_c(T,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], for $T=X,Z,U$.
Use $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ and the ordinary completed-ring kernel right adjoint $J_R=Ri^!_0$ and finite kernel right adjoints $J_n=Ri^!_{0,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint]. Suppose their ambient supported triangles restrict to the integral and finite constructible categories, with canonical ordinary/completed operation comparisons. For every $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ put $K_m=T_{X,m}K$. Here $T_{T,n}L=L\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T$ is reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-derived-tensor]. The canonical direct-image and pullback reduction comparisons carry $T_{X,n}(\eta_{j,K})$ to the finite open unit. There are natural isomorphisms
$$\alpha_{n,K}:T_{Z,n}J_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}J_nT_{X,n}K$$
uniquely characterized by preservation of the exceptional counit, or equivalently by a map of supported triangles with identity middle and open components after the canonical comparisons. For $m\ge n$ let $q_{mn}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ be the canonical quotient map. Define $t_{mn}:J_mK_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}J_nK_n$ as the $i_{*,m}\dashv J_m$ transpose of $q_{mn}\circ\varepsilon_{m,K_m}$, followed by the canonical identification $J_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}J_n$ coming from the scalar-extension/restriction adjunction and closed direct image. The isomorphisms $\alpha_m,\alpha_n$ intertwine the canonical reduction transition of $J_RK$ with this $t_{mn}$. For $r\ge m\ge n$, the composite of the two $t$ maps equals the direct $t_{rn}$ after restriction of scalars, and $t_{nn}=1$. No assertion that arbitrary bounded constructible $A_m$-complexes remain bounded after tensoring with $A_n$ is made. These equalities retain the $A_n$-actions; the comparison of quotient transitions may be made after restricting scalars to the single category with coefficients $A_m$. They are equalities of natural derived morphisms, not merely objectwise isomorphisms.

proof.text: Write $I_a=i_{*,a}$, $V_a=Rj_{*,a}j_a^*$ and $S_{T,mn}=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ on $T$; use $a=R$ for completed coefficients. The ringed open/closed calculus applies since $X$ is noetherian and the complementary open is quasi-compact. The ordinary/completed comparisons are those of [lem-sf-integral-ordinary-recollement-realization]. In particular they give the actual coefficient-linear isomorphisms $c_{n,P}:T_{X,n}I_RP\cong I_nT_{Z,n}P$ and $v_{n,K}:T_{X,n}V_RK\cong V_nK_n$, preserve quotient transitions, and identify $v_{n,K}T_{X,n}(\eta_{j,K})=\eta_{j,K_n}$. This proves the asserted open-unit equation, with its specified normalization. For finite coefficient extension $A_m\to A_n$, denote extension by $L_{T,mn}$. The closed comparison $L_{X,mn}I_m\cong I_nL_{Z,mn}$ is the supported-unit comparison of [lem-sfb-closed-supported-scalar-comparison]. Its hypotheses follow from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and its exact derived descent [lem-sfb-exact-open-closed-unbounded-calculus]. The required inverse-image/scalar comparisons are the actual unit-preserving mates of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], applied to $i$ and $j$. These statements retain the target scalar actions. All these functors are used on their ambient derived categories; constructible restrictions and integral completeness are the hypotheses of the item.

source.place: Integral stage: reduction of the counit and quotient-transition coherence; returned step 7

proof.text:
Define $\alpha_{n,K}$ by the $I_n\dashv J_n$ hom bijection as the transpose of
$$T_{X,n}(\varepsilon_{R,K})\,c_{n,J_RK}^{-1}:I_nT_{Z,n}J_RK\longrightarrow K_n.$$
Thus its defining equation is
$$(*)\qquad\varepsilon_{n,K_n}\,I_n(\alpha_{n,K})=T_{X,n}(\varepsilon_{R,K})\,c_{n,J_RK}^{-1}.$$
The adjunctions and their actual counits are [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint]; the transpose formula and its uniqueness are [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This defines a natural transformation, because both the displayed morphism and the adjunction bijection are natural in $K$. In particular two candidates preserving the counit are equal as derived morphisms, before any scalar restriction.

source.place: Integral stage: reduction of the counit and quotient-transition coherence; returned step 7

proof.text: Apply the exact functor $T_{X,n}$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the assumed integral supported triangle. Using Step 1 it becomes a distinguished triangle with vertices $I_nT_{Z,n}J_RK$, $K_n$, $V_nK_n$. Its second arrow is the finite open unit. Rotate this triangle and the finite supported triangle once. The identity maps on $K_n$ and $V_nK_n$ commute with that arrow, so TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] completes them to a triangle morphism. After rotating back its first component is a map $a:I_nT_{Z,n}J_RK\to I_nJ_nK_n$. Since $i^*I_n\cong1$ [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint], $I_n$ is fully faithful: applying $i^*$ gives the inverse on Hom sets. Write $a=I_n(b)$. The first square says that $b$ satisfies $(*)$, hence $b=\alpha_{n,K}$. The other two components are identities, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $I_n(\alpha_{n,K})$ invertible; applying $i^*$ makes $\alpha_{n,K}$ invertible. Conversely any triangle morphism with those fixed middle and open components satisfies $(*)$, and therefore has this same first component. This proves the claimed equivalent characterization.

source.place: Integral stage: reduction of the counit and quotient-transition coherence; returned step 7

proof.text:
For $N\in D(X,A_n)$ and $P\in D(Z,A_m)$ the closed comparison of Step 1 and the scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,J_mS_{X,mn}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(I_mP,S_{X,mn}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_{X,mn}I_mP,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(I_nL_{Z,mn}P,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,S_{Z,mn}J_nN).$$
The closed adjunctions here are [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint]. Yoneda full faithfulness [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] therefore gives a natural isomorphism $d_{mn,N}:J_mS_{X,mn}N\cong S_{Z,mn}J_nN$. Under the sectionwise identity $I_mS_{Z,mn}=S_{X,mn}I_n$, its normalization is
$$(**)\qquad S_{X,mn}(\varepsilon_{n,N})\,I_m(d_{mn,N})=\varepsilon_{m,S_{X,mn}N}.$$
Indeed the composite Hom bijection sends a map to postcomposition with the right side; the inverse scalar adjunction uses $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(x)$, and the closed comparison has the specified closed-counit normalization. Thus no arbitrary right-adjoint identification is being used. These bijections also show that $h\mapsto S_{X,mn}(\varepsilon_{n,N})I_m(h)$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(P,S_{Z,mn}J_nN)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(I_mP,S_{X,mn}N)$.

source.place: Integral stage: reduction of the counit and quotient-transition coherence; returned step 7

proof.text:
By the closed adjunction, the transpose of $q_{mn}\varepsilon_{m,K_m}$ is $J_m(q_{mn})$: this is the counit naturality equation. Consequently the map specified in the item is exactly
$$t_{mn}=d_{mn,K_n}\,J_m(q_{mn}).$$
Combining counit naturality with $(**)$ gives its useful and unique characterization
$$(***)\qquad S_{X,mn}(\varepsilon_{n,K_n})\,I_m(t_{mn})=q_{mn}\,\varepsilon_{m,K_m}.$$
Uniqueness is the last Hom bijection of Step 4, with $P=J_mK_m$. Every operation is natural, hence so is $t_{mn}$. This is a calculation from the cited adjunction, not a further coefficient-change assertion.

source.place: Integral stage: reduction of the counit and quotient-transition coherence; returned step 7

proof.text:
Put $Q=J_RK$ and let $s_{mn}:T_{Z,m}Q\to S_{Z,mn}T_{Z,n}Q$ be its actual quotient transition. We prove
$$S_{Z,mn}(\alpha_{n,K})s_{mn}=t_{mn}\alpha_{m,K}$$
in $D(Z,A_m)$. Apply the injective Hom correspondence of Step 4, with $P=T_{Z,m}Q$, to both sides. By $(*)$ the image of the left side is
$$S_{X,mn}(T_{X,n}\varepsilon_{R,K})\,S_{X,mn}(c_{n,Q}^{-1})\,I_m(s_{mn}).$$
The closed comparisons preserve actual quotient transitions [lem-sf-integral-ordinary-recollement-realization], so
$$S_{X,mn}(c_{n,Q}^{-1})I_m(s_{mn})=q^{I_RQ}_{mn}c_{m,Q}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of the quotient transition with respect to $\varepsilon_{R,K}$ now makes the image equal to $q_{mn}T_{X,m}(\varepsilon_{R,K})c_{m,Q}^{-1}$. By $(*)$ and $(***)$ this is the image of the right side. For completeness, transition naturality is the termwise tensor identity $(f\otimes1)(1\otimes q)=(1\otimes q)(f\otimes1)$ on K-flat computations: a derived morphism between K-flat complexes is a roof of chain maps through a K-flat complex, the termwise quotient maps commute with chain maps, and clause 2 of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes the reductions and these $A_m$-linear quotient maps independent of the representatives in $D(-,A_m)$ itself; [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined] gives the same independence after restriction to $\mathcal O_E$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection proves the desired equality with its $A_m$ action. No faithfulness of a derived scalar-restriction functor is used.

source.place: Integral stage: reduction of the counit and quotient-transition coherence; returned step 7

proof.text:
All restrictions compose by the identity on underlying module complexes. The precise derived composition and equal-index normalization are [lem-sf-derived-coefficient-sequence-realization]. For $r\ge m\ge n$, compare $S_{Z,rm}(t_{mn})t_{rm}$ and $t_{rn}$ using the injective Hom correspondence of Step 4 for $(r,n)$ and $P=J_rK_r$. Applying $(***)$ first to $(m,n)$ and then to $(r,m)$ gives
$$S_{X,rn}(\varepsilon_{n,K_n})I_r\bigl(S_{Z,rm}(t_{mn})t_{rm}\bigr)=S_{X,rm}(q_{mn})q_{rm}\varepsilon_{r,K_r}=q_{rn}\varepsilon_{r,K_r}.$$
The middle equality is the identity of quotient maps $A_r\to A_m\to A_n=A_r\to A_n$, applied termwise to a K-flat computation; it holds in $D(X,A_r)$ because clause 2 of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes the $A_r$-, $A_m$- and $A_n$-reductions and the termwise quotient maps independent of the K-flat representative, and [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined] gives the same after restriction to $\mathcal O_E$. Equation $(***)$ for $(r,n)$ gives the same image for $t_{rn}$, so the maps agree. At equal indices $q_{nn}=1$ and scalar restriction is the identity; $(***)$ then gives $t_{nn}=1$ by the same injectivity. These are equalities of natural transformations, since every preceding identity holds naturally in $K$. Only reductions of integral objects were tensor-computed; no boundedness claim for arbitrary $A_m$-complexes has entered.
